newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Elkem optimistic despite H1 profit dip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Elkem optimistic despite H1 profit dip.

text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA on Tuesday blamed lower market prices in all its main business areas for a 14 percent drop in first-half pre-tax profits.
Elkem booked six-month profits before tax at 514 million crowns, compared with 598 million crowns for the same 1996 period. Operating profit came to 544 million crowns versus 652 million crowns.
The fall in profits was in line with market expectations, and Elkem's share price was steady in afternoon trade at 154 crowns.

"On the whole, the development in costs has not been as good as expected. Prices and market trends were particularly weak for the manganese operations," the Oslo-based company said in its results communique.
However, second quarter developments for the manganese/chrome business and aluminium were more positive than in the first three months, mainly due to higher market prices.
"In the case of the manganese and chrome business, it was particularly silicon manganese, and to some extent ferrochrome, that saw prices strengthen," Elkem said.
Elkem's other core products showed stable development from the first to second quarters, it said.
The group's captive power production was "normal" in the January to June period.

Although Elkem declined to specify production levels more exactly, it did say generation was 220 gigawatt hours (Gwh) higher than in the first six months 1996 when hydropower reservoir levels fell to abnormally low levels.
Elkem said it expected demand for its products in 1997 to remain at roughly the same level as in 1996.
"In the short term, the market for ferroalloys appears stable. For aluminium, the market has strengthened somewhat during the first part of the third quarter," it said.

It added that a strong dollar was expected to have a positive impact on the year's figures, although currency hedging meant a lag of six months before changes in exchange rates made their full impact.
